source_evidence: Credit rating agencies assign credit ratings based on their evaluation of the risk that the company may default on its bonds.
answer: Credit ratings reflect an agency’s evaluation of a company’s risk of defaulting on its bonds. Default means failing to make timely interest or principal payments. Investment-grade bonds are considered more likely to be paid on time than non-investment-grade bonds. Non-investment-grade bonds are also called high-yield or speculative bonds and generally offer higher interest rates to compensate investors for greater risk. Agencies may review and revise ratings when conditions or expectations change.
